description: Pure, testable care-state logic. Export the hunger cap/threshold from shared, then refactor the mood derivation into an HP-aware pure function and add pure helpers for the hunger/fullness gauge and the caution-threshold check in ui-helpers.ts, all unit-tested in game-ui.test.ts. This is the no-DOM core that FEAT-002 renders. Issue #29 wants the mood (きぶん) derived from hungryLevel/dirty/HP (and isSleeping) as a pure, unit-testable function; it also needs a single source for the hunger cap so the frontend does not hardcode a second copy.
steps: In packages/shared/src/game.ts, change the module-private `const MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL = 10;` to an EXPORTED const: `export const MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL = 10;` (keep the value and all existing uses in applyTimePassage/feed/train unchanged). Because packages/shared/src/index.ts does `export * from './game.ts'`, this makes it importable as `import { MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL } from '@ddm/shared'`. Add a short JSDoc noting it is the single source of truth for the hunger cap shared with the frontend gauge.

Also in packages/shared/src/game.ts, add and export a caution-threshold const for hunger, e.g. `export const HUNGRY_CAUTION_LEVEL = 7;` with JSDoc explaining it is the hungryLevel at/above which the UI should show a caution cue (chosen to match the existing moodLabel 'とてもお腹がすいている' / 'Very hungry' boundary of >=7). Do not change game logic; this const is for the UI only.

Run `npm test` at the shared package (or root) to confirm exporting these consts keeps the shared baseline at 47/47. Optionally add one tiny shared assertion that MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL===10 only if it fits the existing game.test.ts style; otherwise leave shared tests as-is.

In packages/frontend/src/ui-helpers.ts, refactor the mood helpers to be HP-aware. Introduce a pure helper that takes the fields needed to derive mood. Recommended shape: keep the public `moodLabel(monster, lang)` and `moodLabelJa(monster)` names, but WIDEN the accepted monster type from Pick<Monster,'isSleeping'|'dirty'|'hungryLevel'> to also include `stats: Pick<Stats,'hp'|'maxHp'>` (import Stats from '@ddm/shared'). Define the priority order: isSleeping -> dirty -> LOW-HP (new) -> very hungry (hungryLevel>=HUNGRY_CAUTION_LEVEL) -> getting hungry (hungryLevel>=3) -> happy. Place the low-HP branch AFTER sleeping and dirty but BEFORE hunger so a starving/low-HP monster reads as unwell. Use hpPercent(hp,maxHp) and a documented local threshold (e.g. low HP when hpPercent < 30) for the low-HP branch.

Add the new mood strings: JA low-HP e.g. '元気がない' and EN 'Low energy' (or similar short phrase). Keep ALL other JA/EN mood return values byte-identical to today ('すやすや睡眠中'/'Sleeping soundly', 'よごれている'/'Dirty', 'とてもお腹がすいている'/'Very hungry', 'お腹がすいてきた'/'Getting hungry', 'ごきげん'/'Happy'). moodLabel(monster,'ja') must remain byte-identical to moodLabelJa(monster) for every state (the existing byte-identity test must still hold).

Add a pure fullness-gauge helper to ui-helpers.ts, e.g. `fullnessPercent(hungryLevel: number): number` returning Math.round(((MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL - clamped)/MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL)*100) clamped to [0,100], importing MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL from '@ddm/shared' (do NOT hardcode 10). Guard non-finite input to 0 like hpPercent does. Document that 0 hungryLevel => 100% fullness and MAX => 0%.

Add a pure caution helper, e.g. `isHungerCaution(hungryLevel: number): boolean` returning hungryLevel >= HUNGRY_CAUTION_LEVEL (import HUNGRY_CAUTION_LEVEL from '@ddm/shared'). This is what FEAT-002 uses to toggle the caution color/aria on the hunger gauge and badge.

In packages/frontend/src/game-ui.test.ts, update the imports and the SAMPLE_MONSTERS fixture: give each sample a `stats: { hp, maxHp }` so the new signature type-checks, choosing HP so the EXISTING asserted mood outcomes are preserved (e.g. full HP for the non-low-HP cases). Update the existing 'moodLabelJa reflects the monster state in priority order', 'moodLabel(ja) equals moodLabelJa', and 'moodLabel(en) maps the same priority order' tests to pass the stats field; keep their asserted mood strings the same. Add a brief comment in the test file explaining the signature change is intentional (issue #29 makes mood HP-aware).

Add NEW tests in game-ui.test.ts covering: (a) low-HP mood branch for both ja and en (a monster with low hpPercent but not sleeping/dirty yields the low-energy mood); (b) priority ordering (sleeping beats dirty beats low-HP beats hunger); (c) fullnessPercent at hungryLevel 0 (=>100), MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL (=>0), a mid value, and non-finite guard (=>0); (d) isHungerCaution true at >=HUNGRY_CAUTION_LEVEL and false below it. Import MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL/HUNGRY_CAUTION_LEVEL from '@ddm/shared' in the test rather than hardcoding where practical.
Run `cd packages/frontend && npm test` and confirm all tests pass (count rises above the 50 baseline).
acceptance_criteria: MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL and HUNGRY_CAUTION_LEVEL are exported from packages/shared/src/game.ts and importable from '@ddm/shared'; game logic behavior is unchanged.
`npm test` at root keeps shared at 47/47 pass.

moodLabel/moodLabelJa accept HP (via stats) and add a low-HP mood branch placed between dirty and hunger in priority; all previously-asserted mood strings for non-low-HP states remain byte-identical, and moodLabel(m,'ja') === moodLabelJa(m) still holds.
fullnessPercent and isHungerCaution exist as pure helpers, use the shared constants (no hardcoded 10 or 7 in the frontend), and are covered by new tests.
`cd packages/frontend && npm test` passes with the updated existing tests and the new tests (total > 50).
verification: export PATH="/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH" && cd /projects/sandbox/kiro-digitalmonster && npm run build  (green; confirms the StatsPanel call site still compiles after the moodLabel signature change if FEAT-002 not yet done, otherwise defer build check to FEAT-002)
findings:
Implemented. Exported MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL and added HUNGRY_CAUTION_LEVEL=7 (both with JSDoc) in packages/shared/src/game.ts; no game-logic change. ui-helpers.ts: widened mood helpers to a MoodMonster type (adds stats: Pick<Stats,'hp'|'maxHp'>), added a low-HP branch (hpPercent < 30 via local LOW_HP_PERCENT const) between dirty and hunger, strings JA '元気がない' / EN 'Low energy'; all other mood strings byte-identical and moodLabel(m,'ja')===moodLabelJa(m) still holds. Added pure fullnessPercent(hungryLevel) (uses MAX_HUNGRY_LEVEL, non-finite->0, clamped) and isHungerCaution(hungryLevel) (uses HUNGRY_CAUTION_LEVEL); no hardcoded 10/7 in frontend. Tests: updated SAMPLE_MONSTERS fixture + existing moodLabel/moodLabelJa tests with full-HP stats (comment notes issue #29), added new low-HP mood (ja+en), priority ordering, fullnessPercent, and isHungerCaution tests importing the shared constants.

IMPORTANT ENV NOTE for later features: @ddm/shared resolves to its built dist/ (package.json main=dist/index.js), NOT the TS source. After editing packages/shared/src/*.ts you MUST rebuild shared (`npm run build -w @ddm/shared`) before the frontend node:test runner or vite can see new exports; otherwise you get 'does not provide an export named ...'. Verification results: shared `npm test` 47/47 PASS; frontend `npm test` 55/55 PASS (baseline was 50); root `npm run build` GREEN (StatsPanel call site compiled fine since the type was widened, not narrowed, and monster already carries stats). No build caveat; StatsPanel was not touched (belongs to FEAT-002).
